payload.question_text: Which actions can developers perform with the Foundry model catalog? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The catalog lets developers browse available models. It includes first-party, partner, and open-source choices.
Playgrounds and leaderboards support model evaluation. Teams can compare candidates before deployment.
Speech-to-text is an Azure Speech capability. The catalog supports the model-selection lifecycle.
options.better_fit: Choose this when selecting Azure Speech for spoken input.

feedback.intrinsic: This does not perform catalog work.
feedback.instructional: Use Azure Speech for speech conversion.

options.rationale: Foundry supports managing and deploying selected models. Deployment makes a model available to an application.

payload.explanation: Correct. The catalog supports browsing, evaluation, and deployment.

payload.question_text: What can an AI agent do?

options.rationale: Speech conversion is performed by Azure Speech. Agents coordinate broader task workflows.
options.better_fit: Use this description for Azure Speech.

feedback.instructional: Agents can call tools and automate workflows.

options.rationale: Foundry IQ provides knowledge grounding. An agent can use that knowledge while also reasoning and acting.
options.better_fit: Use this description for a knowledge retrieval layer.

feedback.intrinsic: This reduces an agent to retrieval.
feedback.instructional: Agents can use knowledge as part of a workflow.

options.text: Reason, call tools, use data, and automate workflows
options.rationale: An AI agent is task-oriented and reasons over input. It can use data, call tools, and automate work.
Model hosting makes a model available. An agent is the system that coordinates task execution.
options.better_fit: Use this description for model-hosting capability.

feedback.instructional: Hosting and agent behavior are distinct.

payload.explanation: Correct. Agents reason, use data, call tools, and automate work.

payload.question_text: Foundry supports models from first-party, partner, and open-source sources.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry includes first-party, partner, and open-source models.

payload.explanation: Correct. The catalog includes all three source categories.

payload.question_text: Foundry handles message threading, tool execution, safety controls, and observability for agents.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team may over-plan manual coordination.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry manages threads, tool execution, safety, and observability.

payload.explanation: Correct. Foundry manages these agent coordination responsibilities.

payload.question_text: What does agentic retrieval do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Agentic retrieval decomposes a question into subqueries. This helps target retrieval work.
Agentic retrieval searches multiple sources in parallel. This broadens retrieval across connected information.
Agentic retrieval returns relevant information with citations. Citations support traceability.
Text-to-speech is an Azure Speech capability. Retrieval focuses on searching and returning cited information.
options.better_fit: Choose this when describing Azure Speech text-to-speech.

feedback.intrinsic: The app gains voice output but not retrieval.
feedback.instructional: Agentic retrieval decomposes, searches, and cites results.

payload.explanation: Correct. Agentic retrieval decomposes questions, searches sources, and returns citations.

options.text: An Azure resource that provides platform capabilities
options.rationale: A Foundry resource is a narrower Azure component. It is not the overall Microsoft Foundry platform.
options.better_fit: Use this description when defining a Foundry resource.

feedback.instructional: Microsoft Foundry is the broader platform.

options.text: A workspace inside a Foundry resource
options.rationale: A Foundry project is a workspace within a resource. It does not describe the complete platform.
options.better_fit: Use this description when defining a Foundry project.

feedback.intrinsic: This selects the wrong organizational level.
feedback.instructional: A project is a workspace; Foundry is the platform.

options.text: A service used only to store datasets
options.rationale: Foundry supports far more than dataset storage. It supports building, deploying, governing, and managing AI solutions.
options.better_fit: This would fit a data-storage-only service.

feedback.instructional: Foundry supports the AI application lifecycle.

options.text: A platform for building and managing AI apps and agents
options.rationale: Microsoft Foundry is a unified Azure platform for AI applications and agents. It brings together lifecycle capabilities such as models, governance, and monitoring.

payload.explanation: Correct. Foundry is the unified Azure platform for AI applications and agents.

payload.question_text: Foundry IQ enforces user permissions and sensitivity labels so agents return only authorized information.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry IQ enforces permissions and sensitivity labels.

payload.explanation: Correct. Permissions and Purview sensitivity labels restrict returned results.

payload.question_text: Microsoft Foundry is only a workspace inside a Foundry resource.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This assigns Foundry the wrong scope.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry is a platform, while a project is a workspace.

payload.explanation: Correct. A project is the workspace; Foundry is the broader platform.

options.rationale: Azure Vision analyzes images. Foundry IQ connects knowledge sources for grounded answers.

feedback.instructional: Use Vision for images and IQ for knowledge.

options.text: A permission-aware knowledge layer for agents
options.rationale: Foundry IQ is a permission-aware multi-source knowledge layer. It grounds agent answers in organization data.

options.text: A task-oriented system that calls tools
options.rationale: An agent reasons, calls tools, and automates tasks. Foundry IQ provides knowledge that an agent can use.
options.better_fit: Choose this when defining an AI agent.

feedback.intrinsic: The knowledge layer is confused with a worker.
feedback.instructional: Agents act; IQ grounds their answers.

options.rationale: The catalog supports model selection and deployment. Foundry IQ supports knowledge grounding.
options.better_fit: Choose this when selecting or evaluating models.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would seek models instead of sources.
feedback.instructional: Keep model selection distinct from knowledge grounding.

payload.explanation: Correct. Foundry IQ grounds agent answers using permitted knowledge.

payload.question_text: Which are examples of Foundry Tools? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Azure Vision is a Foundry Tool for image analysis. It adds visual understanding to applications.
Foundry IQ is a permission-aware knowledge layer. It is not an individual vision, language, or speech service.
options.better_fit: Choose this for connected, permission-aware knowledge.

feedback.intrinsic: A required AI service may not be added.
feedback.instructional: Vision, Language, and Speech are Foundry Tools.

options.rationale: Azure Language supports language tasks such as summarization and classification. It is a Foundry Tool.
Azure Speech supports speech-to-text and text-to-speech. It is a Foundry Tool.

payload.explanation: Correct. Vision, Language, and Speech are Foundry Tools.

payload.question_text: Foundry IQ creates a knowledge base by storing only public web data.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Foundry IQ supports Blob Storage, SharePoint, OneLake, and public web data.

payload.explanation: Correct. It can combine internal sources with public web data.

payload.question_text: Azure Vision is the Foundry Tool used to convert speech to text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A spoken-input feature would use the wrong service.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Vision analyzes images; Speech converts speech and text.

payload.explanation: Correct. Azure Speech handles speech conversion.

metadata.unit_slo: Identify the Foundry capabilities used to build AI applications and agents.

evaluation_context.goal: Produce an excellent, source-faithful learner session while preserving all deterministic correctness, identity, and sequence constraints.
evaluation_context.source_fidelity_goal: Independently verify the hard-gated edited challenger against the supplied source material. Reject unsupported facts, answers, explanations, feedback, or terminology changes; do not edit the artifact.

criteria.factual_fidelity: Every claim and answer is faithful to the supplied source.
criteria.answer_unambiguity: Each item has one defensible answer under its instructions.
criteria.distractor_plausibility: Distractors are credible without becoming defensible answers.
criteria.misconception_quality: Wrong choices diagnose realistic learner misconceptions.
criteria.cognitive_progression: The ordered session builds understanding at a coherent pace.
criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
criteria.scenario_authenticity: Scenarios resemble credible decisions or tasks.
criteria.feedback_usefulness: Feedback explains the governing concept and next step.
criteria.difficulty_appropriateness: Difficulty matches the stated audience and session position.
criteria.terminology_consistency: Terms are used consistently with the source and across items.
criteria.overall_learner_experience: The exact final sequence is coherent, varied, and instructive.
